statement: At a zoo, an adult ticket costs $3$ dollars more than a child ticket. A family paid $41$ dollars for $2$ adult tickets and $3$ child tickets. What is the price, in dollars, of one adult ticket?

choices.misconception: I assumed all five tickets cost the same and divided 41 dollars by 5.
I solved correctly for the price of a child ticket, 7 dollars, and gave it instead of the adult price.
I wrote the relationship backward as $c = a + 3$, so $2a + 3(a + 3) = 41$ gave $a = 6.40$.

hints: Write the adult price in terms of the child price.
If a child ticket costs $c$ dollars, an adult ticket costs $c + 3$ dollars. Write one equation for the $41$ dollars the family paid.

solutions.reliable: Let $c$ be the child price, so the adult price is $a = c + 3$. Then $2a + 3c = 41$ becomes $2(c + 3) + 3c = 41$, so $5c = 35$, $c = 7$ and $a = 10$. Check: $2(10) + 3(7) = 20 + 21 = 41$. Key idea: when one unknown is described in terms of another, substitute to get a single equation.
solutions.elegant: Take away the extra $3$ dollars on each of the $2$ adult tickets: $41 - 6 = 35$ dollars would buy $5$ child tickets, so a child ticket is $7$ dollars and an adult ticket is $10$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
